subject.title: fix(ollama): remote Ollama streaming stalls at model_call:started on slow hosts

question: Should native Ollama streaming treat provider `timeoutSeconds` as a no-progress timeout while chunks arrive, or must it preserve the current documented total guarded-fetch cap?
rationale: The code shape matches sibling streaming wrappers, but changing a documented provider timeout contract can affect existing user expectations and should be an explicit maintainer choice.

options.title: Accept idle semantics and document it
options.body: Update the Ollama provider docs to describe streaming `timeoutSeconds` as an idle/no-progress timeout and require real remote/slow Ollama proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve a total cap
options.body: Keep or add a separate total guarded-fetch limit while still preventing premature no-progress aborts, then test both behaviors.

options.title: Pause for live root-cause proof
options.body: Keep the PR open until a real affected setup confirms that timeout refresh, not another stream pipeline issue, fixes the stall.

recommendation.title: Accept idle semantics and document it
recommendation.body: Update the Ollama provider docs to describe streaming `timeoutSeconds` as an idle/no-progress timeout and require real remote/slow Ollama proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent provider-runtime, Ollama docs, and guarded-fetch history touching the contract being changed.
